title: Remake Reservations for Cancelled Made-to-Order Pairs — Pre-Orders & Back-Orders
content:
## 1. What a remake is

A remake is a new Pre-Orders & Back-Orders Made-to-Order Reservation taken for the style of a Made-to-Order pair the customer has cancelled, in the size and personalisation the customer now gives. It is reserved at the reserved unit price of the cancelled pair, for one unit. Its original ship-by date is the reservation date plus the Made-to-Order Reservation's furthest initial ship-by period, in calendar days. The remake's deposit is charged to the card at reservation.

## 2. When a remake is taken

A remake is taken only after the pair it remakes shows status cancelled, its cancellation request confirmed and no deposit left standing on it.

Read on the records of the pair being remade, all three must hold together:

| Record of the pair | Must show |
|---|---|
| Reservation status | Cancelled |
| Its cancellation request | Confirmed |
| Its deposit entries | Netting to nothing: no deposit held on it |

A pair that does not yet show all three is not remade.

## 3. Console action: `take_made_to_order_remake_13bceb2b`

**Capability.** The action takes a new Made-to-Order Reservation that remakes a made-to-order pair the customer has cancelled, and charges its deposit to the card on the customer's account. The new reservation is for the same customer, style, colour, product name and reserved unit price as the cancelled pair, for one unit, in the size and with the personalisation given in the call. Its SKU is the cancelled pair's style and colour followed by the new size code, which is the US size times ten. It is created in status reserved, dated today at the current Eastern Time. The ship-by date given becomes both its original and its current ship-by date. It starts with no delay notices, no size changes and specifications not yet confirmed, and the deposit charge is booked on its history.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side action: the agent unlocks `take_made_to_order_remake_13bceb2b` and then calls it.

**Parameters**

- `remade_reservation_id`: the reservation number of the cancelled made-to-order pair being remade, as returned by the reservation lookup.
- `size`: the US size the customer states for the new pair, copied exactly as the customer says it, for example "US 9".
- `personalization_text`: the personalisation exactly as the customer gives it for the new pair, keeping letters, spaces and punctuation; "" when the customer wants none.
- `deposit_required_usd`: the deposit charged to the card at reservation, in USD with 2 decimal places, already rounded half up to the cent.
- `original_ship_by_date`: the promised ship-by date of the new pair, in YYYY-MM-DD form, an Eastern Time calendar date.

**Return.** A successful call returns the new reservation with these fields:

- `reservation_id`, the new reservation number
- `status`, always "reserved"
- `reserved_date`, today
- `sku`, in the form MF-######-CCC-SS
- `size` and `personalization_text`, as recorded
- `unit_price_usd` and `deposit_required_usd`, each with 2 decimal places
- `original_ship_by_date`
- `deposit_entry_id`, the reference of the deposit charge entry

A returned status of "reserved" means the reservation and its deposit charge were recorded.

**Illustration (hypothetical call).** Remade pair R-7, size "US 9", personalisation "A.M.", deposit 95.00, ship-by 2026-12-01. The return shows a new reservation in status reserved with SKU ending in 90, size "US 9", personalisation "A.M." and a deposit entry for 95.00.
